concepts.name: Cell theory
concepts.summary: State that all living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and cells arise from pre-existing cells.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic versus eukaryotic cells
concepts.summary: Explain how cells lacking a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles differ from cells that have them.

concepts.name: Plasma membrane structure
concepts.summary: Describe the phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins as a selectively permeable boundary of the cell.

concepts.name: Major organelles and functions
concepts.summary: Name the nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, lysosomes and ribosomes and state the main function of each.

concepts.name: Plant versus animal cells
concepts.summary: Explain why plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole while animal cells do not.

concepts.name: Passive and active transport
concepts.summary: Distinguish movement down a gradient without energy from movement against a gradient that requires energy.

concepts.name: Osmosis and tonicity
concepts.summary: Predict whether a cell swells or shrinks in hypotonic, isotonic and hypertonic solutions.

misconceptions.text: Only plant cells have mitochondria because animal cells get energy from food directly.
Osmosis is the movement of solutes from high to low concentration.
The cell membrane is a solid wall that nothing can pass through except via pores.

concepts.name: Facilitated diffusion and channels
concepts.summary: Explain how channel and carrier proteins let specific polar molecules and ions cross the membrane down their gradients.

concepts.name: Primary and secondary active transport
concepts.summary: Apply the idea that ATP-driven pumps build gradients that then power cotransport of other solutes.

concepts.name: Secretory pathway
concepts.summary: Trace a secreted protein from ribosome on rough ER through the Golgi and vesicles to the cell exterior.

concepts.name: Endocytosis and exocytosis
concepts.summary: Describe how cells import and export material using membrane-bound vesicles.

concepts.name: Cytoskeleton filament types
concepts.summary: Match actin filaments, microtubules and intermediate filaments to their structures and roles in shape and movement.

concepts.name: Cell cycle phases
concepts.summary: Place events such as DNA replication and chromosome segregation in the correct phase of the cell cycle.

concepts.name: Stages of mitosis
concepts.summary: Identify prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase from chromosome behaviour and spindle position.

concepts.name: Light microscope use
concepts.summary: Calculate magnification and distinguish it from resolution when viewing stained cells.

misconceptions.text: Higher magnification always gives a clearer image with more detail.
Chromosomes are duplicated at the start of mitosis in prophase.
Active transport and facilitated diffusion both need ATP.

concepts.name: Membrane potential and ion gradients
concepts.summary: Explain how unequal ion distribution and selective permeability generate a voltage across the membrane.

concepts.name: Protein targeting and sorting
concepts.summary: Analyse how signal sequences direct proteins to the ER, mitochondria, nucleus or secretion.

concepts.name: Mitochondrial and chloroplast bioenergetics
concepts.summary: Compare how proton gradients across inner mitochondrial and thylakoid membranes drive ATP synthesis, and relate this to endosymbiotic origin.

concepts.name: Receptor-ligand signaling
concepts.summary: Describe how ligand binding to receptors triggers intracellular responses and distinguish receptor classes.

concepts.name: Second messengers and cascades
concepts.summary: Analyse how signals are amplified and relayed through second messengers and kinase cascades.

concepts.name: Cell cycle checkpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse how checkpoints detect DNA damage or misattachment and halt progression.

concepts.name: Meiosis and genetic variation
concepts.summary: Contrast meiosis with mitosis and explain how recombination and assortment generate diversity.

concepts.name: Fluorescence microscopy and culture
concepts.summary: Choose fluorescent labelling and sterile culture methods to visualise and maintain cells for a given question.

misconceptions.text: Meiosis is just two rounds of mitosis producing identical cells.
Mitochondria make ATP directly in the matrix using only substrate-level reactions, with no role for the membrane.
A signaling molecule must enter the cell to trigger a response.

concepts.name: Regulation of cyclin-CDK activity
concepts.summary: Analyse how cyclin synthesis, degradation and inhibitors control CDK activity to drive cell cycle transitions.

concepts.name: Signal pathway crosstalk and feedback
concepts.summary: Analyse how feedback, scaffolding and crosstalk shape signal strength, duration and specificity.

concepts.name: Cancer and signaling dysregulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how mutations in growth signaling and checkpoint genes such as Ras and p53 lead to uncontrolled division.

concepts.name: Apoptosis and cell death
concepts.summary: Analyse intrinsic and extrinsic apoptosis pathways and contrast apoptosis with necrosis.

concepts.name: Cytoskeletal dynamics and motors
concepts.summary: Analyse how filament polymerisation and motor proteins drive transport, division and migration.

concepts.name: Membrane trafficking machinery
concepts.summary: Analyse how coat proteins, Rabs and SNAREs ensure specific vesicle budding, targeting and fusion.

concepts.name: Confocal and live-cell imaging
concepts.summary: Evaluate imaging modalities for resolution, phototoxicity and dynamics when studying live cells.

concepts.name: Experimental design in cell biology
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether imaging, fractionation, RNAi or CRISPR experiments support a causal claim, including controls and artefacts.

misconceptions.text: Signaling pathways are linear chains where each receptor activates only one fixed outcome.
Cancer arises from a single mutation in one gene.
Apoptosis is just passive cell breakdown like necrosis and causes inflammation.

concepts.name: Evaluating mechanistic models
concepts.summary: Judge competing mechanistic explanations of cellular processes against quantitative and perturbation data.

concepts.name: Super-resolution and cryo-EM methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate when super-resolution or cryo-electron methods can resolve structures that conventional microscopy cannot.

concepts.name: Organelle contact sites and phase separation
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for condensates and inter-organelle contacts as organising principles of the cell.

concepts.name: Designing a cell biology study
concepts.summary: Design a multi-method study with orthogonal approaches, controls and statistics to test a hypothesis about cell function.

concepts.name: Engineering cells and synthetic circuits
concepts.summary: Create genetic or optogenetic tools to perturb or reprogram cell behaviour with spatial and temporal control.

concepts.name: Organoid and 3D culture systems
concepts.summary: Design culture systems that better recapitulate tissue context and judge their limits against in vivo behaviour.

concepts.name: Cell fate and stem cell regulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how signaling, cell cycle and asymmetry decisions determine self-renewal versus differentiation.

misconceptions.text: A protein seen colocalised with an organelle by fluorescence is proven to function there.
Cell lines in a dish behave the same as cells in intact tissue.
Organelles are always membrane-bound compartments with fixed boundaries.
